answer: A stake-bonded registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent identity must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed for proven fraud, so a raven-like swarm of fake accounts pays a real price per copy. Reputation then accrues slowly, like sediment building a mesa, and cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker reaching the nadir of their funds finds each new identity costs as much as the last, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes, not one.
